Resolves #18812

🌿 The two lodash advisories stop riding into a published artifact on an accident of tree-shaking — the version consumers receive is patched, and the bundle they receive is 63 KB smaller for it.

Dependabot **#97** (high — code injection via `_.template`) and **#98** (medium — prototype pollution via `_.unset` / `_.omit`) both land on `lodash-es <= 4.17.23`. Nothing in this repository imports lodash.

Evidence: **L1** — resolution and artifact content measured before and after, with a same-command control built on `dev`.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `npm ls lodash-es --all` → **4 × `lodash-es@4.18.1`**, zero at `4.17.23`. `npm install` reports `found 0 vulnerabilities` |
| AC-2 | the AC-1 output is the evidence until the next Dependabot scan closes both alerts |
| AC-3 | `npm run bundle-mermaid` succeeds; `unit/component/MermaidTheme.spec.mjs` 13/13; full `unit` tier **4229 passed / 2 skipped** |
| AC-4 | `package.json` **+1 line**; `package-lock.json` **21 deletions and nothing else** — the three nested `lodash-es` entries, collapsing into the hoisted one |
| AC-5 | the retirement trigger is recorded on #18812 rather than beside the entry — **`package.json` admits no comments**, so the ticket is the only durable home. See below |

## Test Evidence

```
npm ls lodash-es --all      4 x lodash-es@4.18.1        (was 3 x 4.17.23 + 1 x 4.18.1)
npm install                 found 0 vulnerabilities
package-lock.json           21 deletions, 0 insertions  — all three under @chevrotain/*
unit/component/MermaidTheme 13 passed
unit tier                   4229 passed / 2 skipped

bundle size, same command, two trees:
  dev (no override)         5,343,805 bytes
  this head                 5,279,284 bytes   -> 63 KB smaller, three copies deduplicated
```

## Why it ships, which changes the framing

`mermaid` is a devDependency, which normally ends the conversation. It does not here: `.npmignore:81` carries `!/dist/mermaid.mjs`, an explicit **negation**, so the bundle is published, and `src/component/wrapper/Mermaid.mjs` loads it at runtime. The chevrotain code that imports `lodash-es` compiles into an artifact every consumer of `neo.mjs` receives. The honest framing is not "we do not use lodash" but "we ship a bundle containing lodash code".

## Why it is calm rather than urgent — and why that is not a reason to dismiss it

Two measurements, in the tree and in the artifact:

- **Chevrotain imports neither vulnerable function.** Its 27 `lodash-es` import sites pull 36 unique names — `assign clone compact defaults difference drop … pickBy reduce reject some uniq values`. `template`, `unset` and `omit` are absent; it uses `pickBy`, not `omit`. The single `template` hit in its source is the word inside a comment.
- **The shipped bundle contains neither.** `function template`, `function unset`, `function omit`, `baseUnset` → **0 occurrences each** in `dist/mermaid.mjs`, before and after. esbuild shakes out what nothing imports.

So neither advisory is exploitable through this path. **That is the reason this is a calm patch, never a reason to close it unpatched:** the tree-shake is an accident of chevrotain's current import list, and a single patch release that starts using `omit` would put a prototype-pollution sink into a published bundle with the alert already dismissed as not applicable.

## Deltas from ticket

- **The bundle got SMALLER, which I nearly reported as growth.** My first comparison used the `dist/mermaid.mjs` sitting on disk — built 2026-09-13 at 3.45 MB — against a fresh 5.03 MB build, and read a 53% increase. That baseline was a stale artifact, not a control. Building the same command on `dev` gives **5,343,805** bytes against this head's **5,279,284**: the override removes three duplicate copies and takes ~63 KB off what consumers download.
- **AC-5 cannot be satisfied as written.** The ticket asks for the retirement trigger "as a comment beside the entry"; `package.json` is JSON and admits no comments. It lives on #18812 instead, and the trigger is concrete: **retire this override when `mermaid` moves to `chevrotain@13`**, which has no lodash dependency at all.
- **The override is top level, not scoped.** A `chevrotain`-scoped entry reaches only chevrotain's own dependency; two of the three vulnerable copies sit under `@chevrotain/cst-dts-gen` and `@chevrotain/gast`.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Dependabot closes #97 and #98 on its next scan. If either stays open, the resolution is right and the alert is stale — re-measure with `npm ls lodash-es --all` before touching anything else.

Related: Dependabot alerts #97 / #98 · `.npmignore:81` · `buildScripts/build/mermaid.mjs`

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: AC-3's evidence — and the ticket's AC-3 prescription — sits on an axis that cannot see the risk. In mermaid 12.0.0, chevrotain runs only behind `@mermaid-js/parser`, which 15 diagram chunks import (`pie`, `gitGraph`, `info`, `packet`, `radar`, `architecture`, `treeView`, `wardley`, …); `flowDiagram`, `sequenceDiagram` and `classDiagram-v2` are not among them, nor is any shared chunk. Yet `MermaidTheme.spec.mjs` configures a `graph TD` value, `LearnMermaidRender.spec.mjs` renders `learn/` fences, and all 57 `mermaid` fences under `learn/` are `flowchart` / `graph` / `sequenceDiagram` / `classDiagram`. So neither named spec can go red on a chevrotain × `lodash-es@4.18.1` incompatibility. **Discharged here rather than requested:** I walked the relative-import closure of the 36 names chevrotain imports from `lodash-es` (235 files in 4.18.1) and intersected it with the 12 files that differ between the installed 4.17.23 and 4.18.1 copies. Intersection: `compact.js` (comment-only) and `_setCacheHas.js` (`@returns` JSDoc type only). Every other changed file — the advisory sinks `template.js`, `templateSettings.js`, `_baseUnset.js`, plus `fromPairs.js` (now `baseAssignValue`) — sits outside it. Chevrotain executes identical lodash logic on either version, whatever diagram type a consumer renders. Worth carrying: the next override under this bundle needs the same closure check, because a flowchart-only suite can never witness it.
